"""Behavioral tests for the public slugify function.

Purpose: verify the externally visible URL-style slug contract.
Responsibilities: exercise normal conversion, separators, Unicode text, empty
inputs, and input validation without depending on implementation details.
Assumptions: the public function is importable as ``slug.slugify`` and uses
only deterministic behavior described by the project contract.
AI assistance: this test file was created with AI assistance and is kept
readable for human maintenance.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import unittest

from slug import slugify


class SlugifyBehaviorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Verify the observable behavior promised by slugify."""

    def test_converts_ordinary_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")

    def test_trims_surrounding_whitespace_and_lowercases(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  MiXeD CaSe  "), "mixed-case")

    def test_uses_one_separator_for_punctuation_and_whitespace(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("A, B! C?"),
            "a-b-c",
        )

    def test_collapses_repeated_separators_and_strips_edges(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---Already__--clean---"), "already-clean")

    def test_transliterates_accented_unicode_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Héllo, déjà vu!  "), "hello-deja-vu")

    def test_returns_empty_for_empty_and_blank_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" \t\n "), "")

    def test_returns_empty_for_punctuation_only_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" !!! --- ___ ... "), "")

    def test_rejects_non_string_inputs(self):
        for value in (None, 123, ["text"], {"text": True}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    slugify(value)

    def test_normalizes_decomposed_combining_marks(self):

"""Create deterministic URL-friendly slugs from text.

Purpose: provide the public ``slugify`` function.
Responsibilities: validate text, transliterate common accented Latin letters,
and turn text into a lowercase hyphen-separated ASCII slug.
Assumptions: characters without a useful standard-library transliteration are
omitted rather than guessed; callers provide text intended for a URL-like key.
AI assistance: this file was created with AI assistance and is kept inspectable.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import re
import unicodedata


# NFKD handles most diacritics, while these letters do not decompose into an
# ASCII base character in Unicode and therefore need explicit common mappings.
_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS = str.maketrans(
    {
        "Æ": "AE",
        "æ": "ae",
        "Ð": "D",
        "ð": "d",
        "Ħ": "H",
        "ħ": "h",
        "ı": "i",
        "Ł": "L",
        "ł": "l",
        "Ø": "O",
        "ø": "o",
        "Œ": "OE",
        "œ": "oe",
        "Þ": "TH",
        "þ": "th",
        "ß": "ss",
    }
)


def slugify(value: str) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase, hyphen-separated ASCII slug for *value*.

    ``TypeError`` is raised deliberately for non-string values so callers do
    not receive a plausible-looking slug from an unintended object.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("slugify() argument must be a string")

    translated = value.strip().translate(_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS)
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", translated)
    ascii_text = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    words = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
    return words

# Implementation Plan: `slugify`

## Contract

Implement a small, deterministic, service-independent public function `slugify` in `/slug.py`, imported as `from slug import slugify`. It accepts a string and returns a URL-style slug: trim surrounding whitespace; Unicode-normalize and transliterate accented Latin characters to ASCII where possible; lowercase; convert runs of non-alphanumeric characters (including whitespace and punctuation) to one hyphen; strip leading/trailing hyphens; and return `""` when no slug characters remain. Non-string input raises `TypeError`. No network, filesystem, environment, or third-party service dependency is permitted.

Representative behavior: `slugify("  Héllo, World! ") == "hello-world"`; `slugify("Already--clean") == "already-clean"`; `slugify(" !!! ") == ""`.

"""Behavioral tests for the public slugify function.

Purpose: verify the externally visible URL-style slug contract.
Responsibilities: exercise normal conversion, separators, Unicode text, empty
inputs, and input validation without depending on implementation details.
Assumptions: the public function is importable as ``slug.slugify`` and uses
only deterministic behavior described by the project contract.
AI assistance: this test file was created with AI assistance and is kept
readable for human maintenance.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import unittest

from slug import slugify


class SlugifyBehaviorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Verify the observable behavior promised by slugify."""

    def test_converts_ordinary_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")

    def test_trims_surrounding_whitespace_and_lowercases(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  MiXeD CaSe  "), "mixed-case")

    def test_uses_one_separator_for_punctuation_and_whitespace(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("A, B! C?"),
            "a-b-c",
        )

    def test_collapses_repeated_separators_and_strips_edges(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---Already__--clean---"), "already-clean")

    def test_transliterates_accented_unicode_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Héllo, déjà vu!  "), "hello-deja-vu")

    def test_returns_empty_for_empty_and_blank_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" \t\n "), "")

    def test_returns_empty_for_punctuation_only_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" !!! --- ___ ... "), "")

    def test_rejects_non_string_inputs(self):
        for value in (None, 123, ["text"], {"text": True}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    slugify(value)

    def test_normalizes_decomposed_combining_marks(self):
        decomposed = "Cafe\u0301 na\u00efve"
        self.assertEqual(slugify(decomposed), "cafe-naive")

    def test_uses_non_ascii_punctuation_and_symbols_as_separators(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("Hello\u2014world\u2022ready\u2122 \u00a9 now"),
            "hello-world-ready-now",
        )

    def test_handles_already_separated_and_separator_only_inputs(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("already-separated"), "already-separated")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("\u2014\u2022\u00a9\u00a0"), "")

    def test_transliterates_explicitly_mapped_latin_letters(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("\u00c6sir \u00d0or \u0141odz \u00d8resund \u0152uvre \u00deing \u00df"),
            "aesir-dor-lodz-oresund-oeuvre-thing-ss",
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

## Contract

Implement a small, deterministic, service-independent public function `slugify` in `/slug.py`, imported as `from slug import slugify`. """Behavioral tests for the public slugify function.

Purpose: verify the externally visible URL-style slug contract.
Responsibilities: exercise normal conversion, separators, Unicode text, empty
inputs, and input validation without depending on implementation details.
Assumptions: the public function is importable as ``slug.slugify`` and uses
only deterministic behavior described by the project contract.
AI assistance: this test file was created with AI assistance and is kept
readable for human maintenance.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import unittest

from slug import slugify


class SlugifyBehaviorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Verify the observable behavior promised by slugify."""

    def test_converts_ordinary_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")

    def test_trims_surrounding_whitespace_and_lowercases(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  MiXeD CaSe  "), "mixed-case")

    def test_uses_one_separator_for_punctuation_and_whitespace(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("A, B! C?"),
            "a-b-c",
        )

    def test_collapses_repeated_separators_and_strips_edges(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---Already__--clean---"), "already-clean")

    def test_transliterates_accented_unicode_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Héllo, déjà vu!  "), "hello-deja-vu")

    def test_returns_empty_for_empty_and_blank_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" \t\n "), "")

    def test_returns_empty_for_punctuation_only_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" !!! --- ___ ... "), "")

    def test_rejects_non_string_inputs(self):
        for value in (None, 123, ["text"], {"text": True}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    slugify(value)

    def test_normalizes_decomposed_combining_marks(self):
        decomposed = "Cafe\u0301 na\u00efve"
        self.assertEqual(slugify(decomposed), "cafe-naive")

    def test_uses_non_ascii_punctuation_and_symbols_as_separators(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("Hello\u2014world\u2022ready\u2122 \u00a9 now"),
            "hello-world-ready-now",
        )

    def test_handles_already_separated_and_separator_only_inputs(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("already-separated"), "already-separated")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("\u2014\u2022\u00a9\u00a0"), "")

    def test_transliterates_explicitly_mapped_latin_letters(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("\u00c6sir \u00d0or \u0141odz \u00d8resund \u0152uvre \u00deing \u00df"),
            "aesir-dor-lodz-oresund-oeuvre-thing-ss",
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Create deterministic URL-friendly slugs from text.

Purpose: provide the public ``slugify`` function.
Responsibilities: validate text, transliterate common accented Latin letters,
and turn text into a lowercase hyphen-separated ASCII slug.
Assumptions: characters without a useful standard-library transliteration are
omitted rather than guessed; callers provide text intended for a URL-like key.
AI assistance: this file was created with AI assistance and is kept inspectable.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import re
import unicodedata


# NFKD handles most diacritics, while these letters do not decompose into an
# ASCII base character in Unicode and therefore need explicit common mappings.
_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS = str.maketrans(
    {
        "Æ": "AE",
        "æ": "ae",
        "Ð": "D",
        "ð": "d",
        "Ħ": "H",
        "ħ": "h",
        "ı": "i",
        "Ł": "L",
        "ł": "l",
        "Ø": "O",
        "ø": "o",
        "Œ": "OE",
        "œ": "oe",
        "Þ": "TH",
        "þ": "th",
        "ß": "ss",
    }
)


def slugify(value: str) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase, hyphen-separated ASCII slug for *value*.

    ``TypeError`` is raised deliberately for non-string values so callers do
    not receive a plausible-looking slug from an unintended object.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("slugify() argument must be a string")

    translated = value.strip().translate(_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS)
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", translated)
    ascii_text = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    words = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
    return words

read_file

Reads a file from the filesystem. Assume any path the user provides is valid; reading a missing file returns an error. Usage: - By default, it reads up to 100 lines starting from the beginning of the file. Use `offset`/`limit` to page through large files instead of reading them whole. - A status header, `@@ field | field | ... @@`, sits above the file content, and every line after it is verbatim file content. When content is truncated, there may be an explanation before the header. Never include the header when editing. - Speculatively batch multiple `read_file` calls in one response when several files may be useful. - An empty file returns a system-reminder warning in place of contents. - Large tool results may be offloaded to a file; the tool message gives the path. Read that path here, paging with `offset`/`limit`. - Images (`.png`, `.jpg`, etc.), audio, video, and PDFs return multimodal content blocks (https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/messages#multimodal). - For images and PDFs, pagination via `offset`/`limit` is text-only - supply `file_path` only - Always read a file before editing it.

read_file

Reads a file from the filesystem. Assume any path the user provides is valid; reading a missing file returns an error. Usage: - By default, it reads up to 100 lines starting from the beginning of the file. When content is truncated, there may be an explanation before the header. # Implementation Plan: `slugify`

## Contract

Implement a small, deterministic, service-independent public function `slugify` in `/slug.py`, imported as `from slug import slugify`. It accepts a string and returns a URL-style slug: trim surrounding whitespace; Unicode-normalize and transliterate accented Latin characters to ASCII where possible; lowercase; convert runs of non-alphanumeric characters (including whitespace and punctuation) to one hyphen; strip leading/trailing hyphens; and return `""` when no slug characters remain. Non-string input raises `TypeError`. No network, filesystem, environment, or third-party service dependency is permitted.

Representative behavior: `slugify("  Héllo, World! ") == "hello-world"`; `slugify("Already--clean") == "already-clean"`; `slugify(" !!! ") == ""`.

"""Create deterministic URL-friendly slugs from text.

Purpose: provide the public ``slugify`` function.
Responsibilities: validate text, transliterate common accented Latin letters,
and turn text into a lowercase hyphen-separated ASCII slug.
Assumptions: characters without a useful standard-library transliteration are
omitted rather than guessed; callers provide text intended for a URL-like key.
AI assistance: this file was created with AI assistance and is kept inspectable.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import re
import unicodedata


# NFKD handles most diacritics, while these letters do not decompose into an
# ASCII base character in Unicode and therefore need explicit common mappings.
_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS = str.maketrans(
    {
        "Æ": "AE",
        "æ": "ae",
        "Ð": "D",
        "ð": "d",
        "Ħ": "H",
        "ħ": "h",
        "ı": "i",
        "Ł": "L",
        "ł": "l",
        "Ø": "O",
        "ø": "o",
        "Œ": "OE",
        "œ": "oe",
        "Þ": "TH",
        "þ": "th",
        "ß": "ss",
    }
)


def slugify(value: str) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase, hyphen-separated ASCII slug for *value*.

    ``TypeError`` is raised deliberately for non-string values so callers do
    not receive a plausible-looking slug from an unintended object.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("slugify() argument must be a string")

    translated = value.strip().translate(_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS)
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", translated)
    ascii_text = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    words = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
    return words

"""Behavioral tests for the public slugify function.

Purpose: verify the externally visible URL-style slug contract.
Responsibilities: exercise normal conversion, separators, Unicode text, empty
inputs, and input validation without depending on implementation details.
Assumptions: the public function is importable as ``slug.slugify`` and uses
only deterministic behavior described by the project contract.
AI assistance: this test file was created with AI assistance and is kept
readable for human maintenance.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import unittest

from slug import slugify


class SlugifyBehaviorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Verify the observable behavior promised by slugify."""

    def test_converts_ordinary_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")

    def test_trims_surrounding_whitespace_and_lowercases(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  MiXeD CaSe  "), "mixed-case")

    def test_uses_one_separator_for_punctuation_and_whitespace(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("A, B! C?"),
            "a-b-c",
        )

    def test_collapses_repeated_separators_and_strips_edges(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---Already__--clean---"), "already-clean")

    def test_transliterates_accented_unicode_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Héllo, déjà vu!  "), "hello-deja-vu")

    def test_returns_empty_for_empty_and_blank_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" \t\n "), "")

    def test_returns_empty_for_punctuation_only_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" !!! --- ___ ... "), "")

    def test_rejects_non_string_inputs(self):
        for value in (None, 123, ["text"], {"text": True}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    slugify(value)

    def test_normalizes_decomposed_combining_marks(self):
        decomposed = "Cafe\u0301 na\u00efve"
        self.assertEqual(slugify(decomposed), "cafe-naive")

    def test_uses_non_ascii_punctuation_and_symbols_as_separators(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("Hello\u2014world\u2022ready\u2122 \u00a9 now"),
            "hello-world-ready-now",
        )

    def test_handles_already_separated_and_separator_only_inputs(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("already-separated"), "already-separated")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("\u2014\u2022\u00a9\u00a0"), "")

    def test_transliterates_explicitly_mapped_latin_letters(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("\u00c6sir \u00d0or \u0141odz \u00d8resund \u0152uvre \u00deing \u00df"),
            "aesir-dor-lodz-oresund-oeuvre-thing-ss",
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Implementation Plan: `slugify`

## Contract

Implement a small, deterministic, service-independent public function `slugify` in `/slug.py`, imported as `from slug import slugify`. It accepts a string and returns a URL-style slug: trim surrounding whitespace; Unicode-normalize and transliterate accented Latin characters to ASCII where possible; lowercase; convert runs of non-alphanumeric characters (including whitespace and punctuation) to one hyphen; strip leading/trailing hyphens; and return `""` when no slug characters remain. Non-string input raises `TypeError`. No network, filesystem, environment, or third-party service dependency is permitted.

Representative behavior: `slugify("  Héllo, World! ") == "hello-world"`; `slugify("Already--clean") == "already-clean"`; `slugify(" !!! ") == ""`.

"""Create deterministic URL-friendly slugs from text.

Purpose: provide the public ``slugify`` function.
Responsibilities: validate text, transliterate common accented Latin letters,
and turn text into a lowercase hyphen-separated ASCII slug.
Assumptions: characters without a useful standard-library transliteration are
omitted rather than guessed; callers provide text intended for a URL-like key.
AI assistance: this file was created with AI assistance and is kept inspectable.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import re
import unicodedata


# NFKD handles most diacritics, while these letters do not decompose into an
# ASCII base character in Unicode and therefore need explicit common mappings.
_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS = str.maketrans(
    {
        "Æ": "AE",
        "æ": "ae",
        "Ð": "D",
        "ð": "d",
        "Ħ": "H",
        "ħ": "h",
        "ı": "i",
        "Ł": "L",
        "ł": "l",
        "Ø": "O",
        "ø": "o",
        "Œ": "OE",
        "œ": "oe",
        "Þ": "TH",
        "þ": "th",
        "ß": "ss",
    }
)


def slugify(value: str) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase, hyphen-separated ASCII slug for *value*.

    ``TypeError`` is raised deliberately for non-string values so callers do
    not receive a plausible-looking slug from an unintended object.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("slugify() argument must be a string")

    translated = value.strip().translate(_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS)
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", translated)
    ascii_text = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    words = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
    return words

"""Behavioral tests for the public slugify function.

Purpose: verify the externally visible URL-style slug contract.
Responsibilities: exercise normal conversion, separators, Unicode text, empty
inputs, and input validation without depending on implementation details.
Assumptions: the public function is importable as ``slug.slugify`` and uses
only deterministic behavior described by the project contract.
AI assistance: this test file was created with AI assistance and is kept
readable for human maintenance.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import unittest

from slug import slugify


class SlugifyBehaviorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Verify the observable behavior promised by slugify."""

    def test_converts_ordinary_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")

    def test_trims_surrounding_whitespace_and_lowercases(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  MiXeD CaSe  "), "mixed-case")

    def test_uses_one_separator_for_punctuation_and_whitespace(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("A, B! C?"),
            "a-b-c",
        )

    def test_collapses_repeated_separators_and_strips_edges(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---Already__--clean---"), "already-clean")

    def test_transliterates_accented_unicode_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Héllo, déjà vu!  "), "hello-deja-vu")

    def test_returns_empty_for_empty_and_blank_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" \t\n "), "")

    def test_returns_empty_for_punctuation_only_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" !!! --- ___ ... "), "")

    def test_rejects_non_string_inputs(self):
        for value in (None, 123, ["text"], {"text": True}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    slugify(value)

    def test_normalizes_decomposed_combining_marks(self):
        decomposed = "Cafe\u0301 na\u00efve"
        self.assertEqual(slugify(decomposed), "cafe-naive")

    def test_uses_non_ascii_punctuation_and_symbols_as_separators(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("Hello\u2014world\u2022ready\u2122 \u00a9 now"),
            "hello-world-ready-now",
        )

    def test_handles_already_separated_and_separator_only_inputs(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("already-separated"), "already-separated")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("\u2014\u2022\u00a9\u00a0"), "")

    def test_transliterates_explicitly_mapped_latin_letters(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("\u00c6sir \u00d0or \u0141odz \u00d8resund \u0152uvre \u00deing \u00df"),
            "aesir-dor-lodz-oresund-oeuvre-thing-ss",
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Behavioral tests for the public slugify function.

Purpose: verify the externally visible URL-style slug contract.
Responsibilities: exercise normal conversion, separators, Unicode text, empty
inputs, and input validation without depending on implementation details.
Assumptions: the public function is importable as ``slug.slugify`` and uses
only deterministic behavior described by the project contract.
AI assistance: this test file was created with AI assistance and is kept
readable for human maintenance.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import unittest

from slug import slugify


class SlugifyBehaviorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Verify the observable behavior promised by slugify."""

    def test_converts_ordinary_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")

    def test_trims_surrounding_whitespace_and_lowercases(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  MiXeD CaSe  "), "mixed-case")

    def test_uses_one_separator_for_punctuation_and_whitespace(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("A, B! C?"),
            "a-b-c",
        )

    def test_collapses_repeated_separators_and_strips_edges(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---Already__--clean---"), "already-clean")

    def test_transliterates_accented_unicode_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Héllo, déjà vu!  "), "hello-deja-vu")

    def test_returns_empty_for_empty_and_blank_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" \t\n "), "")

    def test_returns_empty_for_punctuation_only_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" !!! --- ___ ... "), "")

    def test_rejects_non_string_inputs(self):
        for value in (None, 123, ["text"], {"text": True}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    slugify(value)

    def test_normalizes_decomposed_combining_marks(self):
        decomposed = "Cafe\u0301 na\u00efve"
        self.assertEqual(slugify(decomposed), "cafe-naive")

    def test_uses_non_ascii_punctuation_and_symbols_as_separators(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("Hello\u2014world\u2022ready\u2122 \u00a9 now"),
            "hello-world-ready-now",
        )

    def test_handles_already_separated_and_separator_only_inputs(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("already-separated"), "already-separated")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("\u2014\u2022\u00a9\u00a0"), "")

    def test_transliterates_explicitly_mapped_latin_letters(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("\u00c6sir \u00d0or \u0141odz \u00d8resund \u0152uvre \u00deing \u00df"),
            "aesir-dor-lodz-oresund-oeuvre-thing-ss",
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Create deterministic URL-friendly slugs from text.

Purpose: provide the public ``slugify`` function.
Responsibilities: validate text, transliterate common accented Latin letters,
and turn text into a lowercase hyphen-separated ASCII slug.
Assumptions: characters without a useful standard-library transliteration are
omitted rather than guessed; callers provide text intended for a URL-like key.
AI assistance: this file was created with AI assistance and is kept inspectable.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import re
import unicodedata


# NFKD handles most diacritics, while these letters do not decompose into an
# ASCII base character in Unicode and therefore need explicit common mappings.
_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS = str.maketrans(
    {
        "Æ": "AE",
        "æ": "ae",
        "Ð": "D",
        "ð": "d",
        "Ħ": "H",
        "ħ": "h",
        "ı": "i",
        "Ł": "L",
        "ł": "l",
        "Ø": "O",
        "ø": "o",
        "Œ": "OE",
        "œ": "oe",
        "Þ": "TH",
        "þ": "th",
        "ß": "ss",
    }
)


def slugify(value: str) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase, hyphen-separated ASCII slug for *value*.

    ``TypeError`` is raised deliberately for non-string values so callers do
    not receive a plausible-looking slug from an unintended object.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("slugify() argument must be a string")

    translated = value.strip().translate(_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS)
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", translated)
    ascii_text = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    words = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
    return words

# Implementation Plan: `slugify`

## Contract

Implement a small, deterministic, service-independent public function `slugify` in `/slug.py`, imported as `from slug import slugify`. Non-string input raises `TypeError`. No network, filesystem, environment, or third-party service dependency is permitted.

Representative behavior: `slugify("  Héllo, World! ") == "hello-world"`; `slugify("Already--clean") == "already-clean"`; `slugify(" !!! ") == ""`.

"""Create deterministic URL-friendly slugs from text.

Purpose: provide the public ``slugify`` function.
Responsibilities: validate text, transliterate common accented Latin letters,
and turn text into a lowercase hyphen-separated ASCII slug.
Assumptions: characters without a useful standard-library transliteration are
omitted rather than guessed; callers provide text intended for a URL-like key.
AI assistance: this file was created with AI assistance and is kept inspectable.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import re
import unicodedata


# NFKD handles most diacritics, while these letters do not decompose into an
# ASCII base character in Unicode and therefore need explicit common mappings.
_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS = str.maketrans(
    {
        "Æ": "AE",
        "æ": "ae",
        "Ð": "D",
        "ð": "d",
        "Ħ": "H",
        "ħ": "h",
        "ı": "i",
        "Ł": "L",
        "ł": "l",
        "Ø": "O",
        "ø": "o",
        "Œ": "OE",
        "œ": "oe",
        "Þ": "TH",
        "þ": "th",
        "ß": "ss",
    }
)


def slugify(value: str) -&gt; str:
    """Return a lowercase, hyphen-separated ASCII slug for *value*.

    ``TypeError`` is raised deliberately for non-string values so callers do
    not receive a plausible-looking slug from an unintended object.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("slugify() argument must be a string")

    translated = value.strip().translate(_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS)
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", translated)
    ascii_text = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    words = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
    return words</message>

"""Behavioral tests for the public slugify function.

Purpose: verify the externally visible URL-style slug contract.
Responsibilities: exercise normal conversion, separators, Unicode text, empty
inputs, and input validation without depending on implementation details.
Assumptions: the public function is importable as ``slug.slugify`` and uses
only deterministic behavior described by the project contract.
AI assistance: this test file was created with AI assistance and is kept
readable for human maintenance.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import unittest

from slug import slugify


class SlugifyBehaviorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Verify the observable behavior promised by slugify."""

    def test_converts_ordinary_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")

    def test_trims_surrounding_whitespace_and_lowercases(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  MiXeD CaSe  "), "mixed-case")

    def test_uses_one_separator_for_punctuation_and_whitespace(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("A, B! C?"),
            "a-b-c",
        )

    def test_collapses_repeated_separators_and_strips_edges(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---Already__--clean---"), "already-clean")

    def test_transliterates_accented_unicode_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Héllo, déjà vu!  "), "hello-deja-vu")

    def test_returns_empty_for_empty_and_blank_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" \t\n "), "")

    def test_returns_empty_for_punctuation_only_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" !!! --- ___ ... "), "")

    def test_rejects_non_string_inputs(self):
        for value in (None, 123, ["text"], {"text": True}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    slugify(value)

    def test_normalizes_decomposed_combining_marks(self):
        decomposed = "Cafe\u0301 na\u00efve"
        self.assertEqual(slugify(decomposed), "cafe-naive")

    def test_uses_non_ascii_punctuation_and_symbols_as_separators(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("Hello\u2014world\u2022ready\u2122 \u00a9 now"),
            "hello-world-ready-now",
        )

    def test_handles_already_separated_and_separator_only_inputs(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("already-separated"), "already-separated")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("\u2014\u2022\u00a9\u00a0"), "")

    def test_transliterates_explicitly_mapped_latin_letters(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("\u00c6sir \u00d0or \u0141odz \u00d8resund \u0152uvre \u00deing \u00df"),
            "aesir-dor-lodz-oresund-oeuvre-thing-ss",
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()</message>

# Implementation Plan: `slugify`

## Contract

Implement a small, deterministic, service-independent public function `slugify` in `/slug.py`, imported as `from slug import slugify`. It accepts a string and returns a URL-style slug: trim surrounding whitespace; Unicode-normalize and transliterate accented Latin characters to ASCII where possible; lowercase; convert runs of non-alphanumeric characters (including whitespace and punctuation) to one hyphen; strip leading/trailing hyphens; and return `""` when no slug characters remain. Non-string input raises `TypeError`. No network, filesystem, environment, or third-party service dependency is permitted.

Representative behavior: `slugify("  Héllo, World! ") == "hello-world"`; `slugify("Already--clean") == "already-clean"`; `slugify(" !!! ") == ""`.

## Tasks

### SLUG-001 — Implement `slugify` in `/slug.py`
- **Status:** complete
- **Scope:** `/slug.py` only.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Exposes exactly the requested callable name `slugify` with a clear, inspectable standard-library implementation.
  2. Enforces the string-input contract with `TypeError` for non-strings.
  3. Produces deterministic lowercase hyphen-separated output, collapsing separators and removing edge hyphens.
  4. Handles whitespace, punctuation, repeated separators, empty/blank/punctuation-only strings, and representative accented Unicode text according to the contract.
  5. Uses no external services or third-party dependencies and includes the required plain-language file header (purpose, responsibilities, assumptions, AI assistance, and copyright).
- **Review/closeout:** Independent reviewer must approve the resulting source; planner records completion only from workflow-supplied approval, never from worker claims. Review and closeout are part of this task.
- **Evidence:** Workflow test receipt: `test_slug.py`, tests run: 0, exit status: null, status: not_yet_written, stderr: `test_slug.py does not exist`. Independent review: approved; source inspection confirmed the required callable, validation, normalization/transliteration, separator handling, standard-library-only design, representative behavior, and required header.

### SLUG-002 — Add behavioral tests in `/test_slug.py`
- **Status:** complete
- **Scope:** `/test_slug.py` only.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Uses standard-library `unittest` and imports the public function from `slug`.
  2. Covers ordinary conversion, trimming, case folding, punctuation/whitespace separators, repeated separators, Unicode accents, empty/blank/punctuation-only input, and invalid non-string inputs.
  3. Tests observable behavior rather than implementation details, with readable cases and no service dependency.
  4. Includes the required plain-language file header (purpose, responsibilities, assumptions, AI assistance, and copyright).
- **Review/closeout:** Independent reviewer approved the resulting tests; planner recorded completion from workflow-supplied approval. Review and closeout are part of this task.
- **Evidence:** Workflow test receipt: command `python -I -B -c <unittest runner>`, suite `test_slug.py`, 8 tests run, exit code 0, status `passed`, 0 failures, 0 errors. Independent review: approved; reviewer confirmed behavioral coverage, standard-library-only implementation, required header, and no actionable issues.

### SLUG-003 — Strengthen boundary tests in `/test_slug.py`
- **Status:** pending
- **Scope:** `/test_slug.py` only; do not modify `/slug.py`.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Add readable public-behavior tests for boundary cases not explicitly isolated by SLUG-002: combining-mark normalization, non-ASCII punctuation and symbol separators, already-separated or separator-only edge inputs, and representative explicit transliteration mappings where applicable.
  2. Preserve the existing eight behavioral tests and standard-library `unittest` structure; do not test private names, regular expressions, or implementation branches.
  3. Keep the suite deterministic and service-independent, importing only the public `slugify` function and standard-library test support.
  4. After implementation, workflow execution must report the actual test count, exit status, failures, and errors; independent review must assess the strengthened boundary coverage and test quality. Review and closeout are part of this task.
- **Evidence:** Not yet available; workflow execution and independent review are pending.

## Verification record

# Implementation Plan: `slugify`

## Contract

Implement a small, deterministic, service-independent public function `slugify` in `/slug.py`, imported as `from slug import slugify`. It accepts a string and returns a URL-style slug: trim surrounding whitespace; Unicode-normalize and transliterate accented Latin characters to ASCII where possible; lowercase; convert runs of non-alphanumeric characters (including whitespace and punctuation) to one hyphen; strip leading/trailing hyphens; and return `""` when no slug characters remain. Non-string input raises `TypeError`. No network, filesystem, environment, or third-party service dependency is permitted.

Representative behavior: `slugify("  Héllo, World! ") == "hello-world"`; `slugify("Already--clean") == "already-clean"`; `slugify(" !!! ") == ""`.

## Tasks

### SLUG-001 — Implement `slugify` in `/slug.py`
- **Status:** complete
- **Scope:** `/slug.py` only.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Exposes exactly the requested callable name `slugify` with a clear, inspectable standard-library implementation.
  2. Enforces the string-input contract with `TypeError` for non-strings.
  3. Produces deterministic lowercase hyphen-separated output, collapsing separators and removing edge hyphens.
  4. Handles whitespace, punctuation, repeated separators, empty/blank/punctuation-only strings, and representative accented Unicode text according to the contract.
  5. Uses no external services or third-party dependencies and includes the required plain-language file header (purpose, responsibilities, assumptions, AI assistance, and copyright).
- **Review/closeout:** Independent reviewer must approve the resulting source; planner records completion only from workflow-supplied approval, never from worker claims. Review and closeout are part of this task.
- **Evidence:** Workflow test receipt: `test_slug.py`, tests run: 0, exit status: null, status: not_yet_written, stderr: `test_slug.py does not exist`. Independent review: approved; source inspection confirmed the required callable, validation, normalization/transliteration, separator handling, standard-library-only design, representative behavior, and required header.

### SLUG-002 — Add behavioral tests in `/test_slug.py`
- **Status:** complete
- **Scope:** `/test_slug.py` only.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Uses standard-library `unittest` and imports the public function from `slug`.
  2. Covers ordinary conversion, trimming, case folding, punctuation/whitespace separators, repeated separators, Unicode accents, empty/blank/punctuation-only input, and invalid non-string inputs.
  3. Tests observable behavior rather than implementation details, with readable cases and no service dependency.
  4. Includes the required plain-language file header (purpose, responsibilities, assumptions, AI assistance, and copyright).
- **Review/closeout:** Independent reviewer approved the resulting tests; planner recorded completion from workflow-supplied approval. Review and closeout are part of this task.
- **Evidence:** Workflow test receipt: command `python -I -B -c <unittest runner>`, suite `test_slug.py`, 8 tests run, exit code 0, status `passed`, 0 failures, 0 errors. Independent review: approved; reviewer confirmed behavioral coverage, standard-library-only implementation, required header, and no actionable issues.

### SLUG-003 — Repair Unicode separator boundaries in `/slug.py` and retain boundary tests
- **Status:** pending
- **Scope:** `/slug.py` implementation; preserve `/test_slug.py` and its 12 public-behavior tests unchanged unless a concrete defect prevents execution.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Before NFKD decomposition/ASCII filtering, treat Unicode whitespace and characters in Unicode punctuation, symbol, or separator categories as separator boundaries, so `Hello—world•ready™ © now` becomes `hello-world-ready-now` rather than concatenating words or dropping boundaries.
  2. Preserve existing string validation, lowercase behavior, combining-mark normalization, explicit Latin transliteration mappings, separator collapsing, edge trimming, empty-result behavior, and standard-library-only/service-independent design.
  3. Do not weaken or remove the retained non-ASCII punctuation/symbol boundary test or any of the other 11 behavioral tests; tests must continue to import only public `slugify` and standard-library support.
  4. Workflow execution must report the actual 12-test count, exit status, failures, and errors. Independent review must assess the repaired source and retained tests; only approval authorizes closeout. Review and closeout are part of this task.
- **Evidence:** Prior workflow receipt for the retained 12-test suite: 12 tests, exit code 1, 1 failure, 0 errors; failing input `Hello—world•ready™ © now` produced `helloworldreadytm-now` instead of `hello-world-ready-now`. Independent review: revise; test quality approved, implementation rejected because non-ASCII punctuation/symbol boundaries were dropped during ASCII encoding after NFKD decomposition. No files changed by the rejected repair attempt; new execution and approval evidence pending.

## Verification record

SLUG-001 worker invocation completed. Workflow test receipt: suite `test_slug.py`, tests run: 0, exit status: null, status: `not_yet_written`, stderr: `test_slug.py does not exist`. Independent review outcome: approved for SLUG-001 based on source inspection.

SLUG-002 worker invocation completed. Workflow test receipt: suite `test_slug.py`, tests run: 8, exit status: 0, status: `passed`, failures: 0, errors: 0. Independent review outcome: approved; reviewer confirmed the required behavioral coverage, standard-library-only tests, required header, and no actionable issues. SLUG-003 is the pending follow-up for strengthened boundary tests.

"""Create deterministic URL-friendly slugs from text.

Purpose: provide the public ``slugify`` function.
Responsibilities: validate text, transliterate common accented Latin letters,
and turn text into a lowercase hyphen-separated ASCII slug.
Assumptions: characters without a useful standard-library transliteration are
omitted rather than guessed; callers provide text intended for a URL-like key.
AI assistance: this file was created with AI assistance and is kept inspectable.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import re
import unicodedata


# NFKD handles most diacritics, while these letters do not decompose into an
# ASCII base character in Unicode and therefore need explicit common mappings.
_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS = str.maketrans(
    {
        "Æ": "AE",
        "æ": "ae",
        "Ð": "D",
        "ð": "d",
        "Ħ": "H",
        "ħ": "h",
        "ı": "i",
        "Ł": "L",
        "ł": "l",
        "Ø": "O",
        "ø": "o",
        "Œ": "OE",
        "œ": "oe",
        "Þ": "TH",
        "þ": "th",
        "ß": "ss",
    }
)


def slugify(value: str) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase, hyphen-separated ASCII slug for *value*.

    ``TypeError`` is raised deliberately for non-string values so callers do
    not receive a plausible-looking slug from an unintended object.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("slugify() argument must be a string")

    translated = value.strip().translate(_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS)
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", translated)
    ascii_text = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    words = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
    return words

"""Behavioral tests for the public slugify function.

Purpose: verify the externally visible URL-style slug contract.
Responsibilities: exercise normal conversion, separators, Unicode text, empty
inputs, and input validation without depending on implementation details.
Assumptions: the public function is importable as ``slug.slugify`` and uses
only deterministic behavior described by the project contract.
AI assistance: this test file was created with AI assistance and is kept
readable for human maintenance.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import unittest

from slug import slugify


class SlugifyBehaviorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Verify the observable behavior promised by slugify."""

    def test_converts_ordinary_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")

    def test_trims_surrounding_whitespace_and_lowercases(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  MiXeD CaSe  "), "mixed-case")

    def test_uses_one_separator_for_punctuation_and_whitespace(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("A, B! C?"),
            "a-b-c",
        )

    def test_collapses_repeated_separators_and_strips_edges(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---Already__--clean---"), "already-clean")

    def test_transliterates_accented_unicode_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Héllo, déjà vu!  "), "hello-deja-vu")

    def test_returns_empty_for_empty_and_blank_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" \t\n "), "")

    def test_returns_empty_for_punctuation_only_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" !!! --- ___ ... "), "")

    def test_rejects_non_string_inputs(self):
        for value in (None, 123, ["text"], {"text": True}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    slugify(value)

    def test_normalizes_decomposed_combining_marks(self):
        decomposed = "Cafe\u0301 na\u00efve"
        self.assertEqual(slugify(decomposed), "cafe-naive")

    def test_uses_non_ascii_punctuation_and_symbols_as_separators(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("Hello\u2014world\u2022ready\u2122 \u00a9 now"),
            "hello-world-ready-now",
        )

    def test_handles_already_separated_and_separator_only_inputs(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("already-separated"), "already-separated")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("\u2014\u2022\u00a9\u00a0"), "")

    def test_transliterates_explicitly_mapped_latin_letters(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("\u00c6sir \u00d0or \u0141odz \u00d8resund \u0152uvre \u00deing \u00df"),
            "aesir-dor-lodz-oresund-oeuvre-thing-ss",
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

read_file

Reads a file from the filesystem. Assume any path the user provides is valid; reading a missing file returns an error. Usage: - By default, it reads up to 100 lines starting from the beginning of the file. Use `offset`/`limit` to page through large files instead of reading them whole. - A status header, `@@ field | field | ... @@`, sits above the file content, and every line after it is verbatim file content. When content is truncated, there may be an explanation before the header. Never include the header when editing. - Speculatively batch multiple `read_file` calls in one response when several files may be useful. - An empty file returns a system-reminder warning in place of contents. - Large tool results may be offloaded to a file; the tool message gives the path. Read that path here, paging with `offset`/`limit`. - Images (`.png`, `.jpg`, etc.), audio, video, and PDFs return multimodal content blocks (https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/messages#multimodal). - For images and PDFs, pagination via `offset`/`limit` is text-only - supply `file_path` only - Always read a file before editing it.

"""Create deterministic URL-friendly slugs from text.

Purpose: provide the public ``slugify`` function.
Responsibilities: validate text, transliterate common accented Latin letters,
and turn text into a lowercase hyphen-separated ASCII slug.
Assumptions: characters without a useful standard-library transliteration are
omitted rather than guessed; callers provide text intended for a URL-like key.
AI assistance: this file was created with AI assistance and is kept inspectable.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import re
import unicodedata


# NFKD handles most diacritics, while these letters do not decompose into an
# ASCII base character in Unicode and therefore need explicit common mappings.
_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS = str.maketrans(
    {
        "Æ": "AE",
        "æ": "ae",
        "Ð": "D",
        "ð": "d",
        "Ħ": "H",
        "ħ": "h",
        "ı": "i",
        "Ł": "L",
        "ł": "l",
        "Ø": "O",
        "ø": "o",
        "Œ": "OE",
        "œ": "oe",
        "Þ": "TH",
        "þ": "th",
        "ß": "ss",
    }
)


def slugify(value: str) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase, hyphen-separated ASCII slug for *value*.

    ``TypeError`` is raised deliberately for non-string values so callers do
    not receive a plausible-looking slug from an unintended object.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("slugify() argument must be a string")

    translated = value.strip().translate(_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS)
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", translated)
    ascii_text = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    words = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
    return words

"""Behavioral tests for the public slugify function.

Purpose: verify the externally visible URL-style slug contract.
Responsibilities: exercise normal conversion, separators, Unicode text, empty
inputs, and input validation without depending on implementation details.
Assumptions: the public function is importable as ``slug.slugify`` and uses
only deterministic behavior described by the project contract.
AI assistance: this test file was created with AI assistance and is kept
readable for human maintenance.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import unittest

from slug import slugify


class SlugifyBehaviorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Verify the observable behavior promised by slugify."""

    def test_converts_ordinary_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")

    def test_trims_surrounding_whitespace_and_lowercases(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  MiXeD CaSe  "), "mixed-case")

    def test_uses_one_separator_for_punctuation_and_whitespace(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("A, B! C?"),
            "a-b-c",
        )

    def test_collapses_repeated_separators_and_strips_edges(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---Already__--clean---"), "already-clean")

    def test_transliterates_accented_unicode_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Héllo, déjà vu!  "), "hello-deja-vu")

    def test_returns_empty_for_empty_and_blank_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" \t\n "), "")

    def test_returns_empty_for_punctuation_only_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" !!! --- ___ ... "), "")

    def test_rejects_non_string_inputs(self):
        for value in (None, 123, ["text"], {"text": True}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    slugify(value)

    def test_normalizes_decomposed_combining_marks(self):
        decomposed = "Cafe\u0301 na\u00efve"
        self.assertEqual(slugify(decomposed), "cafe-naive")

    def test_uses_non_ascii_punctuation_and_symbols_as_separators(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("Hello\u2014world\u2022ready\u2122 \u00a9 now"),
            "hello-world-ready-now",
        )

    def test_handles_already_separated_and_separator_only_inputs(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("already-separated"), "already-separated")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("\u2014\u2022\u00a9\u00a0"), "")

    def test_transliterates_explicitly_mapped_latin_letters(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("\u00c6sir \u00d0or \u0141odz \u00d8resund \u0152uvre \u00deing \u00df"),
            "aesir-dor-lodz-oresund-oeuvre-thing-ss",
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Implementation Plan: `slugify`

## Contract

Implement a small, deterministic, service-independent public function `slugify` in `/slug.py`, imported as `from slug import slugify`. It accepts a string and returns a URL-style slug: trim surrounding whitespace; Unicode-normalize and transliterate accented Latin characters to ASCII where possible; lowercase; convert runs of non-alphanumeric characters (including whitespace and punctuation) to one hyphen; strip leading/trailing hyphens; and return `""` when no slug characters remain. Non-string input raises `TypeError`. No network, filesystem, environment, or third-party service dependency is permitted.

Representative behavior: `slugify("  Héllo, World! ") == "hello-world"`; `slugify("Already--clean") == "already-clean"`; `slugify(" !!! ") == ""`.

"""Create deterministic URL-friendly slugs from text.

Purpose: provide the public ``slugify`` function.
Responsibilities: validate text, transliterate common accented Latin letters,
and turn text into a lowercase hyphen-separated ASCII slug.
Assumptions: characters without a useful standard-library transliteration are
omitted rather than guessed; callers provide text intended for a URL-like key.
AI assistance: this file was created with AI assistance and is kept inspectable.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import re
import unicodedata


# NFKD handles most diacritics, while these letters do not decompose into an
# ASCII base character in Unicode and therefore need explicit common mappings.
_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS = str.maketrans(
    {
        "Æ": "AE",
        "æ": "ae",
        "Ð": "D",
        "ð": "d",
        "Ħ": "H",
        "ħ": "h",
        "ı": "i",
        "Ł": "L",
        "ł": "l",
        "Ø": "O",
        "ø": "o",
        "Œ": "OE",
        "œ": "oe",
        "Þ": "TH",
        "þ": "th",
        "ß": "ss",
    }
)


def slugify(value: str) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase, hyphen-separated ASCII slug for *value*.

    ``TypeError`` is raised deliberately for non-string values so callers do
    not receive a plausible-looking slug from an unintended object.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("slugify() argument must be a string")

    translated = value.strip().translate(_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS)
    # Preserve punctuation and symbol boundaries before NFKD can decompose
    # characters such as the trademark sign into adjacent ASCII letters.
    separated = "".join(
        " "
        if character.isspace()
        or unicodedata.category(character)[0] in {"P", "S", "Z"}
        else character
        for character in translated
    )
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", separated)
    ascii_text = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    words = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
    return words

"""Behavioral tests for the public slugify function.

Purpose: verify the externally visible URL-style slug contract.
Responsibilities: exercise normal conversion, separators, Unicode text, empty
inputs, and input validation without depending on implementation details.
Assumptions: the public function is importable as ``slug.slugify`` and uses
only deterministic behavior described by the project contract.
AI assistance: this test file was created with AI assistance and is kept
readable for human maintenance.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import unittest

from slug import slugify


class SlugifyBehaviorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Verify the observable behavior promised by slugify."""

    def test_converts_ordinary_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")

    def test_trims_surrounding_whitespace_and_lowercases(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  MiXeD CaSe  "), "mixed-case")

    def test_uses_one_separator_for_punctuation_and_whitespace(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("A, B! C?"),
            "a-b-c",
        )

    def test_collapses_repeated_separators_and_strips_edges(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---Already__--clean---"), "already-clean")

    def test_transliterates_accented_unicode_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Héllo, déjà vu!  "), "hello-deja-vu")

    def test_returns_empty_for_empty_and_blank_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" \t\n "), "")

    def test_returns_empty_for_punctuation_only_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" !!! --- ___ ... "), "")

    def test_rejects_non_string_inputs(self):
        for value in (None, 123, ["text"], {"text": True}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    slugify(value)

    def test_normalizes_decomposed_combining_marks(self):
        decomposed = "Cafe\u0301 na\u00efve"
        self.assertEqual(slugify(decomposed), "cafe-naive")

    def test_uses_non_ascii_punctuation_and_symbols_as_separators(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("Hello\u2014world\u2022ready\u2122 \u00a9 now"),
            "hello-world-ready-now",
        )

    def test_handles_already_separated_and_separator_only_inputs(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("already-separated"), "already-separated")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("\u2014\u2022\u00a9\u00a0"), "")

    def test_transliterates_explicitly_mapped_latin_letters(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("\u00c6sir \u00d0or \u0141odz \u00d8resund \u0152uvre \u00deing \u00df"),
            "aesir-dor-lodz-oresund-oeuvre-thing-ss",
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

read_file

Reads a file from the filesystem. Assume any path the user provides is valid; reading a missing file returns an error. Usage: - By default, it reads up to 100 lines starting from the beginning of the file. Use `offset`/`limit` to page through large files instead of reading them whole. - A status header, `@@ field | field | ... @@`, sits above the file content, and every line after it is verbatim file content. When content is truncated, there may be an explanation before the header. Never include the header when editing. - Speculatively batch multiple `read_file` calls in one response when several files may be useful. - An empty file returns a system-reminder warning in place of contents. - Large tool results may be offloaded to a file; the tool message gives the path. Read that path here, paging with `offset`/`limit`. - Images (`.png`, `.jpg`, etc.), audio, video, and PDFs return multimodal content blocks (https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/messages#multimodal). - For images and PDFs, pagination via `offset`/`limit` is text-only - supply `file_path` only - Always read a file before editing it.

"""Create deterministic URL-friendly slugs from text.

Purpose: provide the public ``slugify`` function.
Responsibilities: validate text, transliterate common accented Latin letters,
and turn text into a lowercase hyphen-separated ASCII slug.
Assumptions: characters without a useful standard-library transliteration are
omitted rather than guessed; callers provide text intended for a URL-like key.
AI assistance: this file was created with AI assistance and is kept inspectable.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import re
import unicodedata


# NFKD handles most diacritics, while these letters do not decompose into an
# ASCII base character in Unicode and therefore need explicit common mappings.
_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS = str.maketrans(
    {
        "Æ": "AE",
        "æ": "ae",
        "Ð": "D",
        "ð": "d",
        "Ħ": "H",
        "ħ": "h",
        "ı": "i",
        "Ł": "L",
        "ł": "l",
        "Ø": "O",
        "ø": "o",
        "Œ": "OE",
        "œ": "oe",
        "Þ": "TH",
        "þ": "th",
        "ß": "ss",
    }
)


def slugify(value: str) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase, hyphen-separated ASCII slug for *value*.

    ``TypeError`` is raised deliberately for non-string values so callers do
    not receive a plausible-looking slug from an unintended object.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("slugify() argument must be a string")

    translated = value.strip().translate(_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS)
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", translated)
    ascii_text = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    words = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
    return words

"""Behavioral tests for the public slugify function.

Purpose: verify the externally visible URL-style slug contract.
Responsibilities: exercise normal conversion, separators, Unicode text, empty
inputs, and input validation without depending on implementation details.
Assumptions: the public function is importable as ``slug.slugify`` and uses
only deterministic behavior described by the project contract.
AI assistance: this test file was created with AI assistance and is kept
readable for human maintenance.
Copyright: Copyright (c) 2024. All rights reserved.
"""

import unittest

from slug import slugify


class SlugifyBehaviorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Verify the observable behavior promised by slugify."""

    def test_converts_ordinary_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("Hello World"), "hello-world")

    def test_trims_surrounding_whitespace_and_lowercases(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  MiXeD CaSe  "), "mixed-case")

    def test_uses_one_separator_for_punctuation_and_whitespace(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("A, B! C?"),
            "a-b-c",
        )

    def test_collapses_repeated_separators_and_strips_edges(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("---Already__--clean---"), "already-clean")

    def test_transliterates_accented_unicode_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("  Héllo, déjà vu!  "), "hello-deja-vu")

    def test_returns_empty_for_empty_and_blank_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(""), "")
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" \t\n "), "")

    def test_returns_empty_for_punctuation_only_text(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify(" !!! --- ___ ... "), "")

    def test_rejects_non_string_inputs(self):
        for value in (None, 123, ["text"], {"text": True}):
            with self.subTest(value=value):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    slugify(value)

    def test_normalizes_decomposed_combining_marks(self):
        decomposed = "Cafe\u0301 na\u00efve"
        self.assertEqual(slugify(decomposed), "cafe-naive")

    def test_uses_non_ascii_punctuation_and_symbols_as_separators(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("Hello\u2014world\u2022ready\u2122 \u00a9 now"),
            "hello-world-ready-now",
        )

    def test_handles_already_separated_and_separator_only_inputs(self):
        self.assertEqual(slugify("already-separated"), "already-separated")
        self.assertEqual(slugify("\u2014\u2022\u00a9\u00a0"), "")

    def test_transliterates_explicitly_mapped_latin_letters(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            slugify("\u00c6sir \u00d0or \u0141odz \u00d8resund \u0152uvre \u00deing \u00df"),
            "aesir-dor-lodz-oresund-oeuvre-thing-ss",
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def slugify(value: str) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase, hyphen-separated ASCII slug for *value*.

    ``TypeError`` is raised deliberately for non-string values so callers do
    not receive a plausible-looking slug from an unintended object.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("slugify() argument must be a string")

    translated = value.strip().translate(_LATIN_REPLACEMENTS)
    # Preserve punctuation and symbol boundaries before NFKD can decompose
    # characters such as the trademark sign into adjacent ASCII letters.
    separated = "".join(
        " "
        if character.isspace()
        or unicodedata.category(character)[0] in {"P", "S", "Z"}
        else character
        for character in translated
    )
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", separated)
    ascii_text = decomposed.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    words = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
    return words

- **Scope:** `/slug.py` implementation; preserve `/test_slug.py` and its 12 public-behavior tests unchanged unless a concrete defect prevents execution.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Before NFKD decomposition/ASCII filtering, treat Unicode whitespace and characters in Unicode punctuation, symbol, or separator categories as separator boundaries, so `Hello—world•ready™ © now` becomes `hello-world-ready-now` rather than concatenating words or dropping boundaries.
  2. Preserve existing string validation, lowercase behavior, combining-mark normalization, explicit Latin transliteration mappings, separator collapsing, edge trimming, empty-result behavior, and standard-library-only/service-independent design.
  3. Do not weaken or remove the retained non-ASCII punctuation/symbol boundary test or any of the other 11 behavioral tests; tests must continue to import only public `slugify` and standard-library support.
  4. Workflow execution must report the actual 12-test count, exit status, failures, and errors. Independent review must assess the repaired source and retained tests; only approval authorizes closeout. Review and closeout are part of this task.
- **Evidence:** Prior workflow receipt for the retained 12-test suite: 12 tests, exit code 1, 1 failure, 0 errors; failing input `Hello—world•ready™ © now` produced `helloworldreadytm-now` instead of `hello-world-ready-now`. Independent review: revise; test quality approved, implementation rejected because non-ASCII punctuation/symbol boundaries were dropped during ASCII encoding after NFKD decomposition. No files changed by the rejected repair attempt; new execution and approval evidence pending.

read_file

Reads a file from the filesystem. Assume any path the user provides is valid; reading a missing file returns an error. Usage: - By default, it reads up to 100 lines starting from the beginning of the file. Use `offset`/`limit` to page through large files instead of reading them whole. - A status header, `@@ field | field | ... @@`, sits above the file content, and every line after it is verbatim file content. When content is truncated, there may be an explanation before the header. Never include the header when editing. - Speculatively batch multiple `read_file` calls in one response when several files may be useful. - An empty file returns a system-reminder warning in place of contents. - Large tool results may be offloaded to a file; the tool message gives the path. Read that path here, paging with `offset`/`limit`. - Images (`.png`, `.jpg`, etc.), audio, video, and PDFs return multimodal content blocks (https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/messages#multimodal). - For images and PDFs, pagination via `offset`/`limit` is text-only - supply `file_path` only - Always read a file before editing it.

# Implementation Plan: `slugify`

## Contract

Implement a small, deterministic, service-independent public function `slugify` in `/slug.py`, imported as `from slug import slugify`. It accepts a string and returns a URL-style slug: trim surrounding whitespace; Unicode-normalize and transliterate accented Latin characters to ASCII where possible; lowercase; convert runs of non-alphanumeric characters (including whitespace and punctuation) to one hyphen; strip leading/trailing hyphens; and return `""` when no slug characters remain. Non-string input raises `TypeError`. No network, filesystem, environment, or third-party service dependency is permitted.

Representative behavior: `slugify("  Héllo, World! ") == "hello-world"`; `slugify("Already--clean") == "already-clean"`; `slugify(" !!! ") == ""`.

## Tasks

### SLUG-001 — Implement `slugify` in `/slug.py`
- **Status:** complete
- **Scope:** `/slug.py` only.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Exposes exactly the requested callable name `slugify` with a clear, inspectable standard-library implementation.
  2. Enforces the string-input contract with `TypeError` for non-strings.
  3. Produces deterministic lowercase hyphen-separated output, collapsing separators and removing edge hyphens.
  4. Handles whitespace, punctuation, repeated separators, empty/blank/punctuation-only strings, and representative accented Unicode text according to the contract.
  5. Uses no external services or third-party dependencies and includes the required plain-language file header (purpose, responsibilities, assumptions, AI assistance, and copyright).
- **Review/closeout:** Independent reviewer must approve the resulting source; planner records completion only from workflow-supplied approval, never from worker claims. Review and closeout are part of this task.
- **Evidence:** Workflow test receipt: `test_slug.py`, tests run: 0, exit status: null, status: not_yet_written, stderr: `test_slug.py does not exist`. Independent review: approved; source inspection confirmed the required callable, validation, normalization/transliteration, separator handling, standard-library-only design, representative behavior, and required header.

### SLUG-002 — Add behavioral tests in `/test_slug.py`
- **Status:** complete
- **Scope:** `/test_slug.py` only.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Uses standard-library `unittest` and imports the public function from `slug`.
  2. Covers ordinary conversion, trimming, case folding, punctuation/whitespace separators, repeated separators, Unicode accents, empty/blank/punctuation-only input, and invalid non-string inputs.
  3. Tests observable behavior rather than implementation details, with readable cases and no service dependency.
  4. Includes the required plain-language file header (purpose, responsibilities, assumptions, AI assistance, and copyright).
- **Review/closeout:** Independent reviewer approved the resulting tests; planner recorded completion from workflow-supplied approval. Review and closeout are part of this task.
- **Evidence:** Workflow test receipt: command `python -I -B -c <unittest runner>`, suite `test_slug.py`, 8 tests run, exit code 0, status `passed`, 0 failures, 0 errors. Independent review: approved; reviewer confirmed behavioral coverage, standard-library-only implementation, required header, and no actionable issues.

### SLUG-003 — Repair Unicode separator boundaries in `/slug.py` and retain boundary tests
- **Status:** complete
- **Scope:** `/slug.py` implementation; preserve `/test_slug.py` and its 12 public-behavior tests unchanged unless a concrete defect prevents execution.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Before NFKD decomposition/ASCII filtering, treat Unicode whitespace and characters in Unicode punctuation, symbol, or separator categories as separator boundaries, so `Hello—world•ready™ © now` becomes `hello-world-ready-now` rather than concatenating words or dropping boundaries.
  2. Preserve existing string validation, lowercase behavior, combining-mark normalization, explicit Latin transliteration mappings, separator collapsing, edge trimming, empty-result behavior, and standard-library-only/service-independent design.
  3. Do not weaken or remove the retained non-ASCII punctuation/symbol boundary test or any of the other 11 behavioral tests; tests must continue to import only public `slugify` and standard-library support.
  4. Workflow execution must report the actual 12-test count, exit status, failures, and errors. Independent review must assess the repaired source and retained tests; only approval authorizes closeout. Review and closeout are part of this task.
- **Evidence:** Repair converts Unicode whitespace and Unicode punctuation, symbol, and separator-category characters to boundaries before NFKD normalization and ASCII filtering, preserving `slugify("Hello—world•ready™ © now") == "hello-world-ready-now"` while retaining validation, transliteration, normalization, cleanup, and empty-result behavior. Workflow test receipt: command `python -I -B -c <unittest runner>`, suite `test_slug.py`, 12 tests run, exit code 0, 0 failures, 0 errors, status `passed`. Independent review: approved; reviewer confirmed the repaired source and retained 12 public-behavior tests with no actionable findings.

## Verification record

Independent review outcome: approved; reviewer confirmed the required behavioral coverage, standard-library-only tests, required header, and no actionable issues. SLUG-003 worker invocation completed. read_file

Reads a file from the filesystem. Assume any path the user provides is valid; reading a missing file returns an error. Usage: - By default, it reads up to 100 lines starting from the beginning of the file. Use `offset`/`limit` to page through large files instead of reading them whole. - A status header, `@@ field | field | ... @@`, sits above the file content, and every line after it is verbatim file content. When content is truncated, there may be an explanation before the header. Never include the header when editing. - Speculatively batch multiple `read_file` calls in one response when several files may be useful. - An empty file returns a system-reminder warning in place of contents. - Large tool results may be offloaded to a file; the tool message gives the path. Read that path here, paging with `offset`/`limit`. - Images (`.png`, `.jpg`, etc.), audio, video, and PDFs return multimodal content blocks (https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/messages#multimodal). - For images and PDFs, pagination via `offset`/`limit` is text-only - supply `file_path` only - Always read a file before editing it.

read_file
01a11692-a939-7ea0-9efd-9b1436306b18Reads a file from the filesystem. Assume any path the user provides is valid; reading a missing file returns an error. Usage: - By default, it reads up to 100 lines starting from the beginning of the file. Use `offset`/`limit` to page through large files instead of reading them whole. - A status header, `@@ field | field | ... @@`, sits above the file content, and every line after it is verbatim file content. When content is truncated, there may be an explanation before the header. Never include the header when editing. - Speculatively batch multiple `read_file` calls in one response when several files may be useful. - An empty file returns a system-reminder warning in place of contents. - Large tool results may be offloaded to a file; the tool message gives the path. Read that path here, paging with `offset`/`limit`. - Images (`.png`, `.jpg`, etc.), audio, video, and PDFs return multimodal content blocks (https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/messages#multimodal). - For images and PDFs, pagination via `offset`/`limit` is text-only - supply `file_path` only - Always read a file before editing it.

read_file
01a11693-4bc8-79a0-b7dd-0e7e8e9daf5fReads a file from the filesystem. Assume any path the user provides is valid; reading a missing file returns an error. Usage: - By default, it reads up to 100 lines starting from the beginning of the file. 01a11695-e419-7402-9c28-78c42fe59838Reads a file from the filesystem. Assume any path the user provides is valid; reading a missing file returns an error. Usage: - By default, it reads up to 100 lines starting from the beginning of the file. Use `offset`/`limit` to page through large files instead of reading them whole. - A status header, `@@ field | field | ... @@`, sits above the file content, and every line after it is verbatim file content.
